subject: community-medicine
title: Essential Minerals: Zinc Metabolism, Fluorosis and Calcium

steps.title: Zinc as an essential trace mineral
steps.tx: The divalent trace mineral zinc serves as an indispensable catalytic and structural cofactor for more than three hundred distinct metalloenzymes, including alkaline phosphatase, carbonic anhydrase, alcohol dehydrogenase, and DNA and RNA polymerases. It stabilizes zinc-finger motifs in transcription factors governing cell division and immune cell proliferation, making **zinc metabolic sufficiency** paramount for mucosal repair, linear childhood growth, and normal cell-mediated T-lymphocyte immunity.
steps.say: Zinc is a cofactor for over three hundred enzymes, driving cellular growth, wound healing and immune defence. It stabilizes zinc fingers in DNA to control cell division.

vis.alt: Clinical and biochemical illustration of trace mineral and vitamin deficiencies including zinc acrodermatitis and fluorosis
vis.caption: Trace mineral deficiencies: Periorificial acrodermatitis enteropathica, dental fluorosis mottling, and osteomalacia. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.title: Zinc deficiency: acrodermatitis and childhood diarrhoea
steps.tx: Dietary zinc deficiency is widespread in populations relying heavily on unrefined cereals where dietary phytates chelate zinc into unabsorbable complexes. Manifestations of **clinical zinc deficiency** include stunted linear growth, hypogonadism in adolescent boys, delayed sexual maturation, impaired wound healing, alopecia, blunted taste acuity (hypogeusia), and severe periorificial dermatitis; in infants, the inherited form causes acrodermatitis enteropathica.
steps.say: Zinc deficiency causes stunted height, delayed puberty, hair loss and loss of taste. Diets high in cereal phytates block zinc absorption, causing chronic diarrhoea and rash.

rows: Arrested keratinocyte replication and collagen synthesis
Carbonic anhydrase VI deficiency in taste buds
Suppressed T-cell proliferation and cytokine release
Impaired IGF-1 synthesis and testosterone release

steps.title: Zinc supplementation in acute childhood diarrhoea
steps.tx: Under the Integrated Management of Neonatal and Childhood Illnesses, the national protocol mandates **routine zinc supplementation for diarrhoea** for all children presenting with acute watery diarrhoea. Children aged six months and older receive twenty milligrams of dispersible elemental zinc daily for fourteen consecutive days (ten milligrams daily for infants under six months), cutting diarrhoea duration, stool frequency, and recurrent episodes over the next three months.
steps.say: Give twenty milligrams of zinc daily for fourteen days to all children with diarrhoea. This restores gut lining, stops the diarrhoea sooner, and shields against fresh episodes for three months.

rows: 20% reduction in episode duration; 40% reduction in 3-month recurrences
Repairs damaged intestinal villous brush border

steps.title: Endemic fluorosis: hydrogeology and fluoride ingestion
steps.tx: The geochemical disorder **endemic fluorosis distribution** results from chronic ingestion of excessive fluoride, primarily through deep borehole groundwater leached from fluoride-bearing granite, gneiss and pegmatite rocks across arid Indian states. While an optimal drinking water fluoride level of zero point five to one point zero milligrams per litre protects against dental caries, concentrations exceeding one point five milligrams per litre cause dental and skeletal fluorosis.
steps.say: Drinking deep tubewell water with fluoride over one point five parts per million causes fluorosis. Too much fluoride permanently damages teeth and cripples the spine and joints.

rows: Prevents dental caries; optimal bone health
Safe and wholesome drinking water standard
Dental fluorosis (chalky white patches, brown staining)
Crippling skeletal fluorosis and neurological compression
Permanent physical disability; urgent alternative water

steps.title: Dental fluorosis and Dean's fluorosis index
steps.tx: When excess fluoride is ingested during amelogenesis in the first seven years of life, ameloblasts suffer toxic injury, resulting in **dental fluorosis mottling**. Manifestations are bilateral, symmetrical, and irreversible, progressing from pearly, chalky-white horizontal streaks on dental enamel to confluent brownish-yellow staining, surface pitting, and brittle chipped incisal edges, standardized on Dean's fluorosis index from normal to severe.
steps.say: Drinking high-fluoride water during childhood damages tooth enamel permanently. Chalky-white streaks turn into brown stains, pitting, and brittle, easily broken teeth.

right.title: Severe dental fluorosis
points: Weak, brittle teeth with early attrition

steps.title: Skeletal fluorosis and mechanical crippling
steps.tx: Chronic heavy fluoride ingestion over decades culminates in **skeletal fluorosis progression**, as fluoride replaces hydroxyl ions in hydroxyapatite crystals to form brittle fluorapatite. The skeleton undergoes dense osteosclerosis, cortical thickening, calcification of intervertebral ligaments, sacrotuberous ligaments and tendons, producing agonizing joint stiffness, kyphosis, inability to touch toes or bend the neck, and severe neurological compression.
steps.say: Over decades, fluoride hardens bones into brittle chalk. Spinal ligaments calcify into solid bone, hunching the back and locking the neck into painful, permanent stiffness.

nodes.label: Chronic ingestion of water fluoride > 3 mg/L
Thoracic kyphosis and spinal canal stenosis

steps.title: Defluoridation technologies: Nalgonda technique
steps.tx: Community defluoridation relies on the famous **Nalgonda technique**, an indigenous, cost-effective precipitation method developed by the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI) in Nagpur. The method adds alum (aluminium sulphate) for coagulation, lime (calcium oxide) for accelerated settling and pH adjustment, and bleaching powder for disinfection, precipitating dissolved fluoride as insoluble aluminium complexes that settle as flocculent sludge.
steps.say: The Nalgonda technique treats fluoride-rich water using alum, lime and bleaching powder. The chemicals bind dissolved fluoride into heavy flakes that settle to the bottom, clearing the water.

nodes.label: Raw water with high dissolved fluoride
Sequential addition of alum, lime, bleaching powder
Rapid mixing for 1 min + slow flocculation for 10 min
Sedimentation of sludge; safe supernatant tap water

steps.title: Dietary calcium requirements and bone physiology
steps.tx: Representing the most abundant cation in the human body, **dietary calcium homeostasis** stores ninety-nine percent of bodily calcium in the skeleton and teeth as crystalline hydroxyapatite, with the remaining one percent regulating neuromuscular transmission, cardiac excitation-contraction coupling, and blood coagulation. The ICMR prescribes an adult requirement of one thousand milligrams daily (one thousand two hundred milligrams during pregnancy and lactation), sourced from dairy, ragi, and sesame.
steps.say: Ninety-nine percent of bodily calcium builds the skeleton, while one percent regulates heart rhythm and nerve firing. Adults require one thousand milligrams daily, best obtained from dairy and ragi.

rows: Richest cereal source; excellent weaning food
Extremely dense oilseed source of calcium
Moderate bioavailability due to oxalate binding

steps.title: Osteoporosis prevention and bone mass density
steps.tx: Inadequate calcium and vitamin D intake across childhood and adolescence impairs attainment of peak bone mass, predisposing aging adults to **postmenopausal osteoporosis**. Characterized by low bone mineral density (T-score of minus two point five or less on dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry) and microarchitectural deterioration of trabecular bone, prevention requires weight-bearing exercise, adequate calcium intake, and smoking cessation to prevent devastating hip and vertebral fragility fractures.
steps.say: Building dense bones in youth protects against osteoporosis in later life. Weight-bearing exercise, calcium intake and vitamin D prevent brittle bones and hip fractures in elderly women.

left.title: Normal bone architecture
points: T-score -1.0 or higher on DXA scan
High mechanical resistance to minor trauma

right.title: Osteoporotic bone architecture
points: T-score -2.5 or lower on DXA scan
High susceptibility to low-trauma fragility fractures
